svg.title: Occupancy: which resource runs out first
svg.text: Occupancy: which resource runs out first
one SM of the H200; each coloured box is one resident block of the named kernel

g.text: An SM holds blocks until ONE resource runs out. Solid = blocks that fit together; the red box is the limiter.
occupancy = resident warps ÷ 64 (an SM holds at most 2,048 threads = 64 warps)
register counts: cuobjdump of the committed binaries; occupancy is THEORETICAL (ncu needed root)
mm_tiled_strided<64,32>: 1,024 threads × 32 registers; two 16 KB tiles.
regs: 32 × 1,024 = 32,768 per block → 2 blocks; threads: 2,048 / 1,024 = 2; shared: 228 / 32 ≈ 7
2 blocks × 32 warps = 64 warps → 100% theoretical occupancy (measured 3,635 ms, 19.36 TFLOP/s)
mm_block2d<64,2>: 1,024 threads × 40 registers: the register file fits only one block.
1 block = 32 warps → 50%. Slower than strided (4,263 vs 3,635 ms): same 4 outputs/thread, half the warps.
regs: 64 × 256 = 16,384 → 4 blocks; threads would allow 8; shared ≈ 7
4 blocks × 8 warps = 32 warps → 50%, yet the FASTEST kernel (2,737 ms): more work per thread beats more threads.
flash_forward_kernel (Day 6): 256 threads × 62 registers, 28,800 B dynamic shared memory.
regs: 64 × 256 = 16,384 → 4 blocks; shared: 228 KB / 28.8 KB ≈ 7; threads 8
50% theoretical (occupancy API). Registers limit it, not shared memory (prep pack Q40).
HYPOTHETICAL, not a project kernel: 25% occupancy. Raising R further trades warps for reuse.
